thematic_title: The Pattern Parade — Pattern Rules and Number Patterns to 50
descriptive_title: Grade 1 Mathematics: Algebra (Patterns and Relationships) — Identify, Describe, Translate, and Apply Pattern Rules with Numbers up to 50 (C1.1–C1.4)
short_description: A 5-day Ontario Grade 1 unit on Algebra (C1.1–C1.4), framed as a parade led by Coco the Conductor and four Canadian animals. Children name pattern rules (AB, ABB, AAB, ABC), translate across representations, justify predictions, and build repeating number parades up to 50. Includes 5 lesson plans, 5 worksheets, 7 manipulatives, full assessment suite, and a Junior Pattern Conductor certificate.
long_description:
Take patterns from Kindergarten noticing into Grade 1 reasoning. The Pattern Parade — Grade 1 Edition is a 5-day, ready-to-teach unit that takes children on a journey with Coco the Conductor and the Parade Animals — Bea the Bear, Finn the Fox, Bibi the Beaver, and Moss the Moose — to name pattern rules, translate them across representations, justify their predictions, and finally build repeating number parades using whole numbers up to 50.

Each lesson is fully scripted with teacher prompts, structured for active and partner-rich learning, and includes a printable student worksheet that consolidates the day's thinking. Children build animal parades with manipulatives, name their rules using letter labels, translate one rule into multiple representations (animal, sound, body, number), find missing elements at the start, middle, AND end of broken parades, justify their predictions out loud, and finally lead their own number parade as Junior Pattern Conductors.

What makes this unit different:
- Aligned to all four Ontario Grade 1 Algebra expectations (C1.1, C1.2, C1.3, C1.4) — no gaps, no drift.
- A single coherent narrative across 5 days: recurring characters, threaded vocabulary (pattern, core, rule, predict, justify, extend, missing, translate), an anchor chart that grows day by day.
- Four-track differentiation built into every lesson: emerging learners, extending learners, ELL/IEP, and movement-first learners.
- Detailed teacher script for the conceptually trickiest moments — Lesson 3 (rule translation, the keystone) and Lesson 5 (animals to numbers) — including expected misconceptions and recovery moves.
- A standalone mid-unit formative ('The Same Rule Check') administered between Lesson 3 and Lesson 4 as a 10-minute gate before the unit's hardest content.
- Manipulatives ready to print (default black and white so any classroom printer works), plus reusable assessment trackers per lesson.
- Student-friendly Junior Pattern Conductor certificate for the closing ceremony.

Designed for Canadian classrooms: Canadian animals, the spelling 'colour' throughout, references to familiar Canadian community parades, and Ontario Grade 1 conventions for assessment. The recurring cast (Coco + Bea, Finn, Bibi, Moss) is visually identical to the Kindergarten Pattern Parade unit, so a child returning from K recognizes the characters immediately.

Total classroom time: about 230 minutes across 5 lessons. Teacher prep time: about 105 minutes one-time, then the printables are reusable next year. Suitable for any Grade 1 teacher in Ontario introducing pattern rules and number patterns up to 50, or any teacher building from a Kindergarten patterns base into the Grade 1 expectations.
what_is_included: 5 fully-scripted lesson plans (45–50 minutes each, ~230 minutes total of teaching time)
5 student worksheets aligned to each lesson, with name/date fields, child-voice learning goals, and Grade 1 sentence frames for justification
1 mid-unit formative assessment ('The Same Rule Check') administered between Lesson 3 and Lesson 4
1 end-of-unit reflection sheet with 5 prompts for student self-assessment, including a yes/no audit of all four Grade 1 expectations

7 printable teacher manipulatives: parade animal cards, parade strips (laminated for dry-erase number parades), sound-and-movement cards (6 sets — teacher + 5 partner sets for Lesson 3), missing mystery cards, core loop frames, anchor chart word cards, and a Coco the Conductor puppet
4 class observation trackers: 1 diagnostic (Lesson 1) plus 3 formative (Lessons 2, 3, 4)
1 four-level summative rubric covering all four expectations (C1.1–C1.4) with Grade 1 descriptors
1 summative administration guide tying the worksheet, lesson, and rubric together for the teacher
Junior Pattern Conductor certificate (one per child) for the closing ceremony

Detailed expanded walkthroughs for Lesson 3 (the keystone — translating a rule across representations) and Lesson 5 (animals to numbers up to 50), including expected student misconceptions and teacher recovery moves
Differentiation tracks built into every lesson: emerging learners, extending learners, ELL/IEP, and movement-first learners
target_buyer: Grade 1 teachers in Ontario, or any teacher building from a Kindergarten pattern base into Grade 1 algebra expectations. Especially valuable for teachers who want a coherent multi-day unit that progresses from describing repeating patterns to naming rules, justifying predictions, and translating into number patterns up to 50.
subject: Mathematics
pedagogical_approach: Active, oral-first, movement-rich, with a Grade 1 emphasis on naming rules and justifying predictions out loud. Worksheets are end-of-lesson consolidation, never the main activity. Student-generated patterns are honoured — multiple correct ways to describe the same parade are treated as a strength. Assessment uses a 4-level rubric across each expectation paired with anecdotal observation notes. Number patterns (C1.4) are scaffolded by reusing the same rule labels children practiced with animals all week — the rule does the cognitive work, the numbers add the new layer.
